newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar flat vs yen in directionless Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar flat vs yen in directionless Tokyo.

text.p: 0004 GMT --*Dollar steady vs yen in directionless trade, with activity dull ahead of U.S. Fed policy-setting meeting and Bundesbank's decision on money market rates later in day.

*"Today's focus is on whether the dollar will be able to rise above 118.50 yen," said a dealer at a European bank. "But even if it breaks that, the topside could be limited at around 118.70 yen," he said.
*Downside solid due to mark short-covering vs yen in crosses and buying-on-dip demand below 118 yen. Japanese trading companies might be buying dollars, he added.
*Although dollar recovered to 118 yen overnight, traders were reluctant to keep buying dollars above 118 yen due to fears of sudden fall, as what occurred last week.
*"It is directionless, with the dollar/yen lacking energy to move on its own," said a trust bank dealer.
*Dealers said some Japanese exporters might start selling dollars above 118.50 yen, but their sales would not be in large volumes to keep lid on dollar's rise.
*Dollar rose against mark and yen on Monday in New York, buoyed by impressive turnaround in U.S. stocks and remarks by Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp.
*Krupp said on Monday that rise in German interest rates at present time would be "very damaging" to German economy.
*The remarks dampened speculation that Bundesbank will raise interest rates soon to head off inflationary pressure and stem the mark's excessive fall, helping lift dollar vs mark.
*"With his remarks, we are going back to the previous trend (of a weak mark)," said another trust bank dealer.

*Most operators predicting no changes in Bundesbank's repo rate for its money market operation and in policy at Fed's policy-setting meeting later in day. --Tokyo treasury desk 81-3-3432-1396. email: tokyo.newsroom@reuters.com
